Subject: Deployment pathways: VPC connectivity checklist & next steps

Hi Sam — thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps specific to the deployment mode discussion (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC):

Summary from today
- Avery is leaning toward a Private VPC deployment (data residency and network isolation are primary drivers).
- Key blockers to validate: networking topology, allowlist requirements, and whether PrivateLink or VPC peering is preferred by your infra team.

What Private VPC means for timelines/cost (high-level)
- Hosted API: fastest (hours) but not acceptable for regulated traffic.
- Dedicated capacity: good middle ground (predictable throughput) but won’t meet your VPC isolation requirement.
- Private VPC (what we discussed): requires network work (endpoints/peering), account onboarding, and an initial security review — typical timeline 2–3 weeks from when we have network contacts and AWS account details.

Ask / Network checklist (please share these items so our infra team can prepare):
1) Preferred connectivity method: PrivateLink (AWS NLB endpoint) or VPC peering?
2) AWS account ID(s) we should use to create cross-account resources
3) VPC CIDR ranges and any NAT/egress constraints
4) IP allowlist requirements for outbound traffic to your systems (if any) and inbound rules for our endpoints
5) Network contact (name + email) who can join a technical 30-min sync

I’ve attached an initial questionnaire that captures the above items (initial_network_questions.pdf).

Proposed next steps
- Sam to confirm preferred connectivity method and share AWS account ID + contact (ideally by end of day Monday).
- Rishi (cc’d) will propose a short network call to walk the Avery infra team through the PrivateLink/VPC peering options and required security controls.
- I’ll create a HubSpot milestone and share an onboarding checklist + calendar invite once we have the contact.

If anything above is off, flag it — otherwise I’ll schedule the network sync for next week.

Thanks,

On Sat, Apr 18, 2026 at 11:03 AM Sam Patel <sam.patel@avery-systems.com> wrote:
> We are targeting Private VPC via AWS PrivateLink (we prefer endpoint services to peering for the initial rollout).

Thanks for the details, Sam — this is straightforward. A few technical notes and what we’ll provide from Redwood: 

1) PrivateLink workflow we support
- We host an endpoint service in our customer VPC and request that you create a VPC endpoint (com.amazonaws.vpce). We will share the service name and required NLB configuration.

2) Info we need from your side to create the service
- VPC CIDR(s), subnets (private subnets where the VPCE will be created), and whether the VPC has centralized NAT/egress gateways.
- Security team preference on endpoint policies (wide vs restricted).

3) Allowlist / egress IPs
- For inbound connections to your systems, you should expect our control-plane and data-plane egress IP ranges. We’ll provide a short list of stable egress IPs for firewall rules. Preliminary egress set (subject to change): 54.220.11.21, 34.201.78.10, 3.235.44.99.

4) Certificates and TLS
- We support TLS 1.2+ and can enable mTLS for the data plane if required. If you use a private CA, we’ll need the CA chain for validation.

5) Cross-account IAM
- Not required for PrivateLink itself. We typically rely on endpoint policies + security groups. Cross-account IAM roles are only needed for certain VPC automation scenarios (optional).

6) Timeline and next steps
- Once we have the network contact and AWS account info, we can create the service and share the service name within 48 business hours. End-to-end onboarding typically completes in ~2 weeks (network setup + validation + security review).

I attached our PrivateLink setup guide for your network team (private_link_setup_guide.md). I’ll propose a short agenda for the technical sync: service name + NLB ports, subnet selection, security group rules, and validation steps.

Cheers,
